title: Career Roadmap: Cloud Engineer
summary: A Cloud Engineer designs, deploys, manages, secures, and maintains computing infrastructure and applications hosted on cloud platforms. Cloud engineers help organisations run software reliably without managing every physical server themselves.

facts.Current degree: BS in Computer Science & Data Analysis

blocks.text: A Cloud Engineer designs, deploys, manages, secures, and maintains computing infrastructure and applications hosted on cloud platforms. Cloud engineers help organisations run software reliably without managing every physical server themselves.
They work with virtual machines, storage, networks, databases, containers, automation, monitoring, security, and cloud-native services.

rows.text: BS in Computer Science & Data Analysis
Cloud Support Associate, Junior Cloud Engineer, Cloud Operations Trainee

This is a suggested learning sequence, not the official semester structure of the degree. Adjust it to the programme's actual curriculum and duration.
Stage 1 — Programming and IT fundamentals

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: First year
Learn

items.text: Python programming, functions, modules and exception handling.
Data structures, algorithms and basic problem-solving.
Linux commands, files, permissions and process management.

blocks.label: Networking fundamentals
blocks.text: IP addresses, DNS, HTTP/HTTPS, TCP/IP and ports.

items.text: SQL, relational databases and basic data modelling.
Git, GitHub and basic software development workflows.
Operating-system concepts, virtualisation and server fundamentals.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Write Python scripts to automate file and system tasks.
Install and use Linux in a virtual machine.
Build a small database-backed application.
Diagnose basic DNS, connectivity and permission problems.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Understand how applications, operating systems, networks and databases work together.
Stage 2 — Cloud platform fundamentals

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Second year
Learn

blocks.label: Cloud service models
blocks.text: IaaS, PaaS and SaaS.

items.text: Public, private, hybrid and multi-cloud concepts.
Compute instances, object storage, block storage and managed databases.
Virtual networks, subnets, routing, firewalls and load balancing.
Identity and access management (IAM), roles and least-privilege access.
Availability zones, backups, fault tolerance and disaster recovery.
Billing, budgets, resource tagging and cloud cost management.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Create a cloud virtual machine and secure remote access.
Host a static website using object storage or a suitable hosting service.
Deploy a basic application with a managed database.
Configure permissions, logs and budget alerts.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Deploy and manage basic cloud resources securely on one cloud platform.
Stage 3 — Automation and cloud-native development

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Third year
Learn

items.text: Shell scripting and more advanced Python automation.
Docker images, containers and container registries.
Infrastructure as Code using Terraform or a provider-native equivalent.
CI/CD pipelines and automated testing.
Monitoring, logs, metrics, alerts and troubleshooting.
Kubernetes fundamentals after becoming comfortable with containers.
Cloud security, secret management, patching and vulnerability basics.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Containerise a web application and deploy it to the cloud.
Automate infrastructure provisioning using Terraform.
Set up a CI/CD pipeline that tests and deploys an application.
Configure monitoring and test recovery from a service failure.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Automate the deployment and operation of a small application.
Stage 4 — Production readiness and job preparation

blocks.label: Suggested period
blocks.text: Final learning phase
Learn

items.text: High availability, scaling and resilient architecture.
Infrastructure monitoring and incident response.
Backup restoration and disaster-recovery testing.
Cloud security architecture and audit logs.
Cost optimisation and resource utilisation.
Networking troubleshooting and performance diagnosis.
Technical documentation, runbooks and operational handovers.

blocks.text: Practical activities

items.text: Deploy a complete application with separate application and data layers.
Configure monitoring, alerts, backups and access restrictions.
Document an outage scenario and demonstrate recovery.
Complete a cloud or DevOps internship and prepare for technical interviews.

blocks.label: Milestone
blocks.text: Demonstrate that you can deploy, secure, monitor and troubleshoot a cloud-hosted application.
Start with one platform and develop transferable concepts before learning another.

blocks.label: Recommended approach
blocks.text: Learn one cloud platform deeply enough to deploy and troubleshoot real applications. Avoid trying to master AWS, Azure and Google Cloud simultaneously at the beginning.
Build projects that demonstrate infrastructure, automation, security and operational reliability.

blocks.label: Project 1
blocks.text: Cloud-hosted website

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Beginner

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Deploy a static website using an appropriate cloud hosting service.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Storage configuration, access permissions, DNS or hosting configuration, HTTPS where supported, and basic cost awareness.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Architecture diagram, deployment steps, screenshots, configuration notes and a teardown guide.

blocks.label: Project 2
blocks.text: Secure cloud application

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Deploy a small application with an application layer and a managed database.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Virtual networking, IAM, environment variables or secret management, backups, logging and access restrictions.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Architecture diagram, deployment scripts, access model, monitoring setup and recovery instructions.

blocks.label: Project 3
blocks.text: Automated deployment pipeline

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Intermediate

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Containerise an application and create a CI/CD pipeline that tests and deploys it.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Git workflows, automated testing, Docker, deployment automation and safe handling of credentials.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Source code, pipeline configuration, build logs, deployment instructions and rollback procedure.

blocks.label: Project 4
blocks.text: Cloud monitoring and recovery lab

blocks.label: Level
blocks.text: Advanced

blocks.label: Build
blocks.text: Deploy a sample service, configure monitoring and alerts, and test how it recovers from a simulated failure.

blocks.label: Demonstrate
blocks.text: Logs, metrics, alert thresholds, backup restoration, incident diagnosis and reliability improvements.

blocks.label: Deliverables
blocks.text: Monitoring dashboard, incident report, recovery test results and a runbook.
For every project, publish a README, architecture diagram, setup instructions, test evidence and estimated operating costs. Never publish cloud access keys, passwords, private keys or other secrets.
Remember to shut down or delete billable resources after completing a lab. Set budget alerts where available, and review the provider's current pricing before deploying.
Begin applying when you can demonstrate a Linux environment, basic networking knowledge and at least one working cloud deployment.

blocks.text: Actual eligibility varies by employer. Some engineering roles may require particular degree backgrounds or experience, so check individual job descriptions against the BS programme's accepted qualifications.
Potential areas for further study include:

items.text: Cloud computing and distributed systems.
Computer science and software engineering.
Cybersecurity and cloud security.
DevOps, platform engineering and site reliability.
Data engineering and cloud-based analytics.
Distributed databases and large-scale systems.
Artificial intelligence infrastructure and MLOps.

blocks.text: Admission requirements vary. Verify whether a programme accepts the specific BS qualification, and check prerequisites, entrance tests and any required undergraduate subjects.
Stage 1 — Cloud Support or Junior Cloud Engineer
Learn resource provisioning, permissions, troubleshooting, monitoring and operational procedures.
Stage 2 — Cloud Engineer
Own infrastructure deployments, automation, service reliability and routine cloud architecture decisions.
Stage 3 — Senior or Specialist Engineer
Design resilient systems and specialise in DevOps, security, networking, platform engineering or reliability.
Stage 4 — Cloud Architect, Platform Lead or Engineering Manager
Lead architecture, infrastructure strategy, technical standards or engineering teams.
Progression depends on practical ability, system complexity, experience, business needs and leadership skills rather than years of service alone.

Cloud Engineer readiness
0 of 12
Write basic Python and shell scripts
Use Linux commands, permissions, processes and logs
Explain DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP, ports, subnets and routing
Deploy a virtual machine or application on one cloud platform
Configure cloud identity and least-privilege access
Deploy and connect a cloud-hosted database
Use Git and document infrastructure changes
Containerise an application with Docker
Automate infrastructure provisioning with Terraform or an equivalent tool
Configure monitoring, alerts and a basic recovery procedure
Complete at least two documented cloud projects
Prepare a technical résumé and practise cloud troubleshooting interviews
A job-ready graduate should be able to:

items.text: Explain cloud computing architecture and service models.
Use Linux, networking and scripting to solve infrastructure problems.
Deploy and secure basic cloud-hosted applications.
Configure identities, storage, virtual networks and databases.
Automate infrastructure and application deployments.
Monitor systems, diagnose failures and document recovery procedures.
Understand basic cloud cost management and security practices.
Demonstrate skills through a reproducible portfolio and technical interviews.

blocks.label: Recommended priority
blocks.text: Start with Linux, networking and Python, then learn one cloud platform's compute, storage, networking and identity services. Add Terraform and Docker after completing a working deployment. Focus on projects that demonstrate secure configuration, troubleshooting and automation rather than collecting certifications alone.
